summary.headline: Emcure FY26 revenue crossed INR9,204 crore (+16.6%), but Q4 domestic growth slowed to 5.2% on Zuventus disruption; FY27 guided to low-to-mid-teen growth.
summary.overview: Emcure reported FY26 revenue of INR9,204 crore (+16.6% YoY), with adjusted PAT up 41% to INR1,008 crore and EBITDA margin up 80 bps to 19.4%. Q4 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,470 crore, but domestic growth slowed to 5.2% because of attrition and restructuring at the newly consolidated Zuventus business. International markets grew 25.7% in Q4, with Europe and Canada leading. Management said April is on plan and guided FY27 to low-to-mid-teen revenue growth and 75-100 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY; margin up from 18.4% in Q4 FY25
Up YoY due to Manx payouts and Zuventus minority stake buyout

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR4,027 crore (+10%), led by women's health, cardio, CNS and oncology. Q4 revenue INR977 crore (+5.2%) was hit by Zuventus. Management said ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% and the full-year ex-Zuventus base growth was high single digit.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR5,177 crore (+22.2%). Q4 revenue INR1,493 crore (+25.7%); currency added roughly 7-8% overall, about 11-12% in Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,850 crore (+25.5%). Q4 revenue INR538 crore (+35.8%), helped by Manx and Amphotericin B. Management expects mid-teens CAGR over the next two years.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,487 crore (+18.7%). Q4 revenue INR399 crore (+28.6%), driven by market share gains and launches.

segments.name: Rest of World / Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 ROW revenue INR1,840 crore (+21.8%), with ARV and non-ARV both contributing. Q4 emerging markets revenue INR556 crore (+15.5%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid-teens.
EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps in FY27, assuming stable regulations, macro conditions and no major geopolitical upheaval.
Domestic target: grow faster than industry (8-9% expected), at low double-digits.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
FY27 average currency assumption of INR92/USD.
Gross margin expected to stay around 60% for the full year.
Employee expense growth expected at about 10% in FY27 versus about 7% in FY26.
Canada semaglutide launch via Dr. Reddy's partnership in Quebec, expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
Field force around 4,000 MRs; about 40% sit in Zuventus. Field productivity rose from INR5.4 lakh to INR7 lakh per MR over two years.
Amphotericin B launched in select European markets in H2 FY26; expansion to Europe and rest of world planned for FY27.
Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar endorsed by CDSCO SEC; launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval.
Lenacapavir: DMF filed; product registration sought in FY27.
demand_pricing: Zuventus: Q4 restructuring (new management after October minority buyout, portfolio and team reorganisation) drove high field attrition; management says April is on plan. Normal MR attrition is 20-30%.

Poviztra (Novo Nordisk rDNA semaglutide, India exclusive): early uptake promising after April 2026 price cut; about 1,000 sales reps promoting it. Management says the product is differentiated versus synthetic generics.
In-licensed products make up about 15% of domestic sales. The Roche nephrology brands (2-3 key brands) are under INR50 crore annualised with no upfront payment.
Market share in covered markets was roughly flat for FY26 after the Q4 impact.

Raw material and solvent prices have risen with the Middle East conflict. Freight and insurance costs are also up. Company holds 1-2 quarters of inventory and says there are no supply issues yet. IPA is seeking a domestic price hike.
Canada: Dr. Reddy's partnership via Mantra subsidiary in Quebec, where pricing is expected to be more favourable. Apotex and Reddy's received semaglutide approvals recently.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Zuventus impact on India growth and whether restructuring will weigh on the next few quarters.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year ex-Zuventus base growth would have been 9-10%, and Q4 ex-Zuventus was below 8%. It expects the impact to fade, with April back on track.

qa_highlights.question: What operational synergies are expected from Zuventus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing synergies are limited because the plants serve different products. Gains are expected in sales and marketing organisation and support functions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 domestic growth outlook and the currency assumption behind guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth is expected at 8-9% and Emcure aims for low double digits. The guidance assumes INR92/USD.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and geopolitical cost pressure is in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory covers 1-2 quarters, so impact is limited near term. Management said guidance includes current pricing, and the industry is facing solvent and freight cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Canada semaglutide path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Quebec partnership with Dr. Reddy's aims for an early launch around Q2 FY27, and its own filing will target the rest of Canada in the medium term. Deal terms were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Emcure open to more in-licensing deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is organic growth but in-licensing will continue where it is accretive.

risks_watch: Zuventus recovery: whether April's on-plan trend holds through Q1 FY27 after high attrition.
Poviztra price war and whether market share recovers after the April 2026 price cut.
Raw material, solvent, freight and insurance inflation if the Middle East conflict persists beyond the 1-2 quarters of inventory.
Rising debt (net debt INR1,054 crore) after the Manx and Zuventus payouts.
Q4 Mantra earn-out exceptional charge of INR43 crore, which was above initial expectations.
Currency: a weaker rupee supports international revenue, but the INR92/USD assumption needs monitoring.
summary.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on FY27 and on the Zuventus recovery, though Q4 domestic softness was openly acknowledged. Management was noticeably evasive on monthly April growth and on the semaglutide market-share recovery. It was also cautious on cost pressures, saying the impact is hard to quantify.
key_quotes: FY26 marked the start of our 5-year strategy, focusing on turning last year's operational changes into measurable outcomes.
Ex of the Zuventus impact for the full year would have been close to the 9% - 10% base business growth that we have been talking about, that we delivered even in the first 9 months.
I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9% , and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

In FY27, we project low to mid -teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic conditions.

adds.what: FY27 capex of INR400-425 crore (capacity not specified; capex only, no named plant or line)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to low-to-mid-teens (midpoint about 12.5%) with 75-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion; backing is partial: Poviztra and Canada semaglutide launches, Europe Amphotericin B/Manx, Bevacizumab H1 FY27 launch pending approval, and a 4,000-MR field force, but no specific capacity or order numbers, and FY27 capex of INR400-425 crore has no stated capacity.

mgmt.note: Zuventus saw new management after its October minority buyout; management is reorganising portfolio and team, but no named top-management change or growth stance was detailed in the brief.
initiatives: Portfolio and team reorganisation at Zuventus
